Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of what I heard you care most about:
- End-to-end p95/p99 for user-facing calls (token length ~300–600)
- Sustained concurrency of ~200 qps with spikes to 500 qps during peak windows
- Streaming compatibility (chunked responses, low first-byte latency) for audio-captioning UI
- Deterministic failover to fallback model when capacity constrained

Highlights from the demo: Redwood hosted API gave good interactive feel; you wanted us to put numbers against what we saw and compare to your current provider (CortexAI).

Proposed acceptance thresholds (for discussion with your infra/QA):
- p95 end-to-end <= 150 ms for a 512-token response (network+inference+post-processing)
- p99 end-to-end <= 450 ms for same profile
- Sustained throughput: handle 200 qps with 95% success at the above SLOs
- Burst handling: graceful degradation but keep p95 <= 350 ms under 500 qps for short bursts (<=60s)
- Streaming: first byte (initial chunk) <= 80 ms, subsequent chunk cadence <= 40 ms per chunk (50 token chunks)

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a small perf snapshot (sample traffic shape) and any firewall/egress constraints (your infra team).
2) We run a 48-hour smoke test comparing Redwood hosted vs CortexAI using a mirrored traffic shape (we'll provide test harness).
3) Engineering from both sides align on the test plan and acceptance matrix; post-test we review results and map to pricing/commit.

If that sounds right, could you: (a) confirm the acceptance thresholds above, (b) send the sample perf CSV and a point-of-contact for infra/QA?

I attached a short SLO proposal (spreadsheet) that maps test scenarios to pass/fail gates.

Best,
Tessa

Tessa —

Thanks for the forward and the clear ask. I reviewed nimble_perf_snapshot.csv and sketched a practical test plan and acceptance matrix below. High level: hosted can beat CortexAI in most realistic configs, but the long-tail (800–1200 tokens) and streaming first-byte latency are the gating factors.

Quick feasibility notes:
- Baseline kernels: use optimized attention kernels + int8 quant at 16k context for the long-tail; this gives best p95 while keeping cost down.
- Batching: configure adaptive batching with max latency 8 ms for streaming-enabled routes; for non-streaming we can increase window to 12–16 ms to improve throughput.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (helps mid/long tokens).
- Network: we assume <=30 ms of network hop inside US region; we'll isolate network vs runtime by marking timestamps at client-proxy, proxy->provider and post-process.

Proposed acceptance matrix (pass if all gates pass):
- Gate A (short/mid): for <=600 tokens at sustained 200 qps, p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 400 ms.
- Gate B (long-tail): for 800–1200 tokens at same throughput mix, p95 <= 320 ms, p99 <= 800 ms (we will debate p99 but propose this as initial threshold).
- Gate C (burst): under 500 qps bursts (<=60s), p95 <= 350 ms for mixed-workload; p99 <= 900 ms.
- Gate D (streaming): first-byte <= 80 ms; subsequent chunks <= 50 ms latency cadence for 50-token chunks.

Test harness & metrics we will produce:
- Synthetic replay of their 24h qps trace (we'll provide loader) with real token size distribution buckets.
- Per-request timing breakdown: T_client_send, T_proxy_enter, T_provider_first_byte, T_provider_last_byte, T_postprocess, total_e2e.
- p50/p95/p99 by token bucket and aggregated, plus error-rate and CPU/GPU utilization.

Operational recommendations to present in the report:
- Suggest starting test on our hosted eu-west/US-west pools simultaneously and report both; route production per their traffic geography later.
- Recommend a canary run (1 hour) then a 48-hour full run for stable stats.
- Expose two knobs to Nimble: batching window (ms) and quant profile (int8/int16) via the SLO proposal spreadsheet.

Deliverables and timeline (if Nimble approves):
- Day 0: confirm windows and provide credentials/network egress info.
- Day 1: run canary (1 hour) — deliver preliminary p95/p99 by bucket.
- Day 2–3: 48-hour full run — deliver final report and recommendation (includes cost delta vs CortexAI).

I'm comfortable with the acceptance matrix above as a first pass; we can tighten Gate B/C after seeing initial numbers. Karthik — please call out anything I'm missing (quantization caveats, batch sizing tradeoffs).

Marcus
